header: Date: 2026-08-05 | Start: 16:30 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Kapoor (Praxis CTO), Lena Ortiz (ML Engineer), Priya Rao (Security), Diego Ramos (Product)
summary: Intro discovery for Praxis AI migration off OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Main concerns: eval parity, compatibility with vLLM/TGI pipelines, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS requirements, SOC2/auditability. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, and security docs; schedule technical deep dive.
topics: vLLM / TGI compatibility and model-parity testing
Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Maya our SE. Quick intros, Samir?
00:12 Samir Kapoor: Yeah hi all, Samir here, CTO at Praxis. We've been running most production calls on OpenAI gpt-4.x, some Anthropic for safety checks, and experimenting with vLLM on prem for cost reasons.
00:25 Maya Chen: cool, thanks. quick high level - are you looking to move fully off OpenAI or hybrid?
00:30 Samir Kapoor: Mostly move critical latency-sensitive workloads to Dedicated, keep some of the low-risk helper flows on hosted providers while we validate. Cost and predictability are the drivers.
00:42 Lena Ortiz: we also run a local TGI stack for a few models, but it's brittle across updates; tokenization differences bite us sometimes.
00:50 Jordan Patel: right, that's common. two things we usually focus on: API compatibility (we map to OpenAI-like endpoints) and eval parity - so outputs line up with what you're used to.
01:05 Priya Rao: security questions upfront - VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs are musts. Also SSO/SAML for team access.
01:18 Jordan Patel: totally, Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC options supports KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SAML/SCIM - we'll share the security pack.
01:30 Diego Ramos: can you speak to model versions? we rely on the exact family and tokenizer for some evaluation prompts.
01:36 Maya Chen: we keep a model catalog - you can pin model versions. For tokenizer parity, often it's about using the same tokenizer binary or a compatible mapping; in our benchmarks we run token-level diffs to spot shifts.
01:50 Samir Kapoor: about vLLM/TGI - we use vLLM for low-latency streaming and TGI for local hosting. Compatibility worries us: will the same prompts produce same answers on Redwood Dedicated?
02:05 Maya Chen: good question. short answer: usually yes for the same model weights and tokenizers, but quantization and kernel selection can change subtle behavior. our benchmark plan runs a parity suite: 1k prompts, deterministic seeds, and compares top-k/token distributions.
02:28 Lena Ortiz: what's your typical latency for a 2048 token context on Dedicated? we need under 250ms first-token for chat.
02:35 Maya Chen: depends on hardware and batching; for a single-request, single-stream on A100/8GPU pools we've seen 120-220ms first-token for 2k context with optimized kernels and KV warm. But if you're batching heavily latency shifts.
02:52 Samir Kapoor: and tokens/sec throughput for embeddings + generation? we're doing 30M tokens/month.
02:58 Jordan Patel: for throughput, Dedicated can do tens of millions depending on cluster size. we'll propose sizing. cost per token is usually better than hosted at scale, but it depends on your concurrency and burst profile.
03:18 Priya Rao: on data residency - we need EU-only for some customers, do you support region pinning?
03:24 Jordan Patel: yes, region pinning and private deployments in VPC regions; Private deployments can be entirely within your cloud account.
03:30 Samir Kapoor: about rollouts: we want canary + automatic fallback to hosted if Dedicated capacity is constrained. is that supported?
03:37 Maya Chen: yes, smart routing supports policy-based routing: latency-first, cost-first, or fallback tiers. canary and A/B rollouts are supported in Console.
03:45 Diego Ramos: any gotchas with fine-tuned models? we fine-tune locally and push variants.
03:50 Maya Chen: you'll want to standardize training/adapter formats; we support SFT and LoRA-style adapters in our model onboarding, but we validate with the parity suite. sometimes quantization for inference requires re-eval.
04:10 Samir Kapoor: walk through the migration steps?
04:14 Jordan Patel: typical flow: 1) sizing and pricing, 2) model parity tests run by SE with your prompts, 3) pilot on Dedicated with a subset of traffic (canary), 4) cutover and ops handoff.
04:28 Lena Ortiz: who runs the parity tests? internal or Redwood?
04:31 Maya Chen: SE-led but collaborative - we'll run initial tests with your snippets and provide scripts so you can run them in your environment (vLLM/TGI) for apples-to-apples.
04:45 Samir Kapoor: transcripts sometimes show weird tokens when we move to quantized models; how do you debug generation regressions?
04:52 Maya Chen: we store token-level logs in the eval harness, diff outputs, and we have rollback to fp16 models. also suggestion: don't quantize initial pilot models until parity is validated.
05:05 Priya Rao: what's your SOC2 status and how fresh are the reports?
05:09 Jordan Patel: Redwood is SOC2 Type II as of Q2 2026; we'll attach the cert and summary.
05:15 Priya Rao: and pen-tests?
05:18 Jordan Patel: annual pen-tests, can share the executive summary.
05:22 Diego Ramos: any automation for batching / KV cache tuning? we have highly variable prompt lengths.
05:28 Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize recommends batching configs and cache policies; we can supply suggested batch sizes per workload and the Console shows token-level cost impact. for variable length, continuous batching with a max latency SLO helps.
05:45 Samir Kapoor: if we run a pilot, what metrics should we measure?
05:48 Maya Chen: latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, output quality (BLEU/ROUGE or custom evals), and error rates (timeouts, OOMs). also track KV cache hit rates.
06:05 Lena Ortiz: we have stuck points: some prompts hit the system message length and cause truncation; how do you manage sequence length differences?
06:12 Maya Chen: we can recommend model variants and kernel configs; also suggest prefix compression or longer-context variants. we'll include seq-length profiling in the parity tests.
06:25 Samir Kapoor: are there compatibility layers for OpenAI API keys, or do we need to refactor code?
06:30 Jordan Patel: Redwood's API is OpenAI-compatible for common endpoints, but for advanced features (like private endpoints + custom routing) you'll add config flags. migration effort depends on how much you use undocumented behaviors.
06:45 Priya Rao: curious about encryption at rest - does Redwood allow customer-managed KMS?
06:50 Jordan Patel: yes, customer-managed KMS and HSM options on Private/Dedicated.
07:00 Diego Ramos: do you have any shared artifact for benchmark scripts?
07:04 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share a repo with the parity harness, sample prompts, and instructions for running locally on vLLM/TGI.
07:12 Samir Kapoor: what about latency variability under burst? our usage spikes dramatically during business hours.
07:18 Maya Chen: Dedicated supports burst capacity patterns with autoscaling policies and reserved pool. for very spiky workloads we advise a mix of Dedicated + hosted fallback for excess traffic.
07:35 Jordan Patel: price-wise we'll show committed vs on-demand. committed capacity gets predictable lower per-token cost.
07:42 Samir Kapoor: any upfront migration costs?
07:45 Jordan Patel: small onboarding professional services for pilot setup if you want Redwood to help do the parity runs and infra provision, otherwise self-serve is possible.
07:55 Priya Rao: about logging - how long do you retain audit logs? we need at least 12 months for some regs.
07:59 Jordan Patel: default is 90 days; extended retention add-on can cover 12+ months. we'll include that in the security doc.
08:10 Lena Ortiz: can we test with our fine-tuned models first?
08:14 Maya Chen: yes - we can onboard your tuned weights; we'll run a validation pass. may ask you to share artifacts via secure S3 or private repo.
08:22 Samir Kapoor: ok let's recap next steps - Jordan?
08:25 Jordan Patel: I'll send pricing and a Dedicated sizing proposal by end of week; Maya will send the parity harness and scripts and proposes a target test matrix; Praxis to share prompts and traffic profile; Priya to confirm compliance asks and we'll attach SOC2 + pen-test summaries.
08:40 Samir Kapoor: sounds good, thanks.
08:43 Diego Ramos: thanks everyone.
08:45 Jordan Patel: thanks all - we'll follow up in email with dates for deep dive.
08:50 (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), some speaker attribution may be approximate; timestamps are rough markers every ~30-90s.
